bug_description.original: Use-of-uninitialized-value in _decode_pkcs12_auth_safe at lib/x509/pkcs12.c:67:6, detected by MemorySanitizer via fuzz target gnutls_pkcs12_key_parser_fuzzer.
bug_description.normalized: In _decode_pkcs12_auth_safe, a stack-allocated char buffer oid[MAX_OID_SIZE] (128 bytes) is declared without initialization at line 53. The function calls asn1_read_value to read the authSafe.contentType OID from the parsed PKCS12 structure into oid. For a crafted PKCS12 input containing a minimal single-byte OID (0x20, encoding "0.32"), asn1_read_value returns ASN1_SUCCESS and writes a short value to oid without null-terminating the buffer. The code reserves one byte for null-termination (len = sizeof(oid) - 1) but never explicitly writes oid[len] = '\0' after the read. The subsequent strcmp(oid, DATA_OID) at line 67 reads past the 5 initialized bytes into uninitialized stack memory, triggering MemorySanitizer's use-of-uninitialized-value detection.

source.description: Reads the attacker-controlled contentType OID from the parsed PKCS12 ASN.1 structure into the stack-allocated oid buffer. For the crafted input containing a minimal single-byte OID (0x20), asn1_read_value returns ASN1_SUCCESS and writes a short value to oid without null-terminating the buffer, leaving bytes from offset 5 onward uninitialized.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled PKCS12 DER input; the authSafe.contentType field contains a single-byte OID (06 01 20) that decodes to a short string without null-termination.

sink.description: strcmp reads oid which has 5 initialized bytes at offsets 0-4 followed by uninitialized stack memory. Since oid is not null-terminated after the initialized portion, strcmp reads past it into uninitialized bytes at offset 5. MSan detects use-of-uninitialized-value at this comparison against DATA_OID ("1.2.840.113549.1.7.1", 21 bytes including null).

root_cause.description: The 128-byte stack buffer oid is declared without initialization. The code at line 59 reserves one byte for null-termination (len = sizeof(oid) - 1) but never writes oid[len] = '\0' after asn1_read_value fills the buffer. When asn1_read_value writes data without null-termination for an edge-case OID input, the remaining bytes stay uninitialized and are read by the subsequent strcmp call.

tainted_value_origin.description: The pkcs12 parameter is the parsed ASN.1 tree derived from the attacker-controlled PKCS12 DER input. It carries the crafted authSafe.contentType OID that drives asn1_read_value's behavior, causing incomplete initialization of the oid buffer.

coarse_trace.summary: Iterates through PKCS12 bags in a loop, calling gnutls_pkcs12_get_bag for each index to extract bag contents from the imported PKCS12 structure.
Calls _decode_pkcs12_auth_safe to decode the authenticatedSafe container from the PKCS12 structure before parsing individual bag entries.

Reads the authSafe.contentType OID from the ASN.1 tree into a stack-allocated buffer via asn1_read_value, then compares it with DATA_OID using strcmp. For a crafted minimal OID input, the buffer is not null-terminated after the read, causing strcmp to access uninitialized stack memory.

fine_trace.note: Allocates 128-byte stack buffer oid without initialization. MAX_OID_SIZE is 128 (defined in x509_int.h:34). All 128 bytes contain indeterminate values. The code later reserves one byte for null-termination (line 59: len = sizeof(oid) - 1 = 127) but never writes the null terminator explicitly.

Reads the contentType OID from the parsed PKCS12 ASN.1 structure into oid. For the crafted input containing a single-byte OID (DER: 06 01 20, encoding OID "0.32"), asn1_read_value returns ASN1_SUCCESS and writes a short value to the first few bytes of oid. The function does not null-terminate the written data for this edge-case input, leaving bytes from offset 5 onward in the 128-byte buffer uninitialized.

Guard checks only the asn1_read_value return code. Since asn1_read_value returned ASN1_SUCCESS, the condition is false and the early-return path is not taken. The guard does not verify that oid is a properly null-terminated string — the missing oid[len] = '\0' between this guard and the subsequent strcmp is the initialization gap.

strcmp compares oid against DATA_OID ("1.2.840.113549.1.7.1", 21 bytes including null). oid has 5 initialized bytes at offsets 0-4 but no null terminator, so strcmp reads past the initialized portion into uninitialized stack memory at offset 5. MSan detects use-of-uninitialized-value. The sanitizer reports: "Uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memcmp at offset 5 inside [0x7ffd1ea93140, 21)".

depends_on.via: oid buffer with partially initialized content from asn1_read_value

parser_admitted.description: gnutls_pkcs12_import successfully parses the 13-byte crafted DER input as a PKCS12 structure (returns >= 0), allowing execution to proceed to gnutls_pkcs12_simple_parse which eventually calls _decode_pkcs12_auth_safe where the vulnerability is triggered.

allocation_context.description: MSan attributes the uninitialized allocation to the stack frame of _decode_pkcs12_auth_safe at line 52 (function entry). The actual declaration char oid[MAX_OID_SIZE] is at line 53.

format.name: DER
format.contract: A 13-byte DER-encoded PKCS12 structure containing a minimal authSafe.contentType OBJECT IDENTIFIER encoded as a single byte (06 01 20, OID "0.32"). The structure must be valid enough for gnutls_pkcs12_import to accept it (outer SEQUENCE with version INTEGER and authSafe ContentInfo SEQUENCE), but the edge-case single-byte OID causes asn1_read_value to produce a non-null-terminated value in the oid buffer.
